title: Companion-agent memory guardrails become binding rules in a second major market by Q4 2027
body: China's Interim Measures for the Administration of AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services, issued in April 2026 and taking effect July 15, 2026, became the first live regime to treat persistent-identity emotional-companion agents as a regulated product surface, and ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen resolved compliance over the July 3-6 weekend by switching the features off rather than redesigning them. Qwen is disabling humanlike interactive and user-created agents on July 10 and broader agent services on July 15, while Doubao pulls its agent feature July 15 and gives users until October 15 to export data before it is unrecoverable. The load-bearing detail is the shape of the mandate, not the shutdown: the rules require anti-addiction systems, in-session usage notifications, and instant-exit mechanisms, and they carve out customer-service, knowledge-Q&A, workplace, and education tools that lack the sustained emotional-companion framing. That draws a precise, copyable regulatory line around exactly the capabilities the agent-harness field has been racing to add, long-horizon memory and a consistent cross-session persona, and it does so in enforceable statute with a hard effective date rather than a consultation draft. The same consumer-harm concerns that motivated it, minor safety, dependency, and disclosure of machine identity, are already live in EU AI Act transparency obligations, in US state proposals on companion chatbots, and in ongoing scrutiny of youth-facing AI companions elsewhere. Expect a second major jurisdiction to convert that concern into a binding instrument, a statute, enacted rule, or enforceable code, that imposes companion-specific guardrails on emotional-companion or persistent-memory agents: mandated machine-identity disclosure, anti-addiction or usage-limit controls, and a data-export-or-deletion path on shutdown, tracking the same emotional-companion scope carve-out China drew. The coupling is that a live enforced template plus overlapping consumer-protection pressure turns companion-AI memory and persona from a product-design choice into a regulated surface in more than one market, and vendors keep resolving the tension by withdrawal or scope-narrowing rather than by building compliant persistence.

reasoning.because: China's April 2026 anthropomorphic-AI rules take effect July 15; Doubao and Qwen pulled companion agents to comply
reasoning.given: Rules mandate anti-addiction, usage alerts, instant-exit and scope out non-companion tools; EU/US echo the concern
reasoning.so_that: A second major jurisdiction enacts a binding instrument imposing companion-specific memory, disclosure and exit guardrails
reasoning.landing: by Q4 2027, a second market enacts binding companion-AI guardrails on persistent-memory agents
reasoning.plain_language: China now legally limits AI friend apps that remember you, so another big country will likely pass its own rules on them soon.

summary: China's Interim Measures on AI anthropomorphic interaction take effect July 15, 2026, and ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen withdrew persistent-memory companion agents rather than redesign them to meet anti-addiction, usage-alert, and instant-exit mandates. With EU and US consumer-protection pressure echoing the same concern, expect a second major jurisdiction to enact binding companion-AI guardrails on emotional-companion or persistent-memory agents by Q4 2027.
